name: r4-m10
statement: In Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math, the early RL steps (100-400) concentrate the policy on the base's own high-probability paths, which raises accuracy on finished answers. The lower entropy also makes T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 sampling cross top-p's lock threshold more often, so looping cap hits rise above the base's. Only the slower pressure of 3.1's truncation-as-negative training later removes these loops, so cap hits at T 0.6 rise and then fall over training (base < step 100-400, step 2,800 far below the base).
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B (base) and Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math checkpoints step_0100, step_0400 and step_2800 (main), sampled at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 with a 16,384-token cap, plain prompt mainly. Also covers the cued prompt at step 400 and the harder set (clean 328) at step 400. Measured quantities: cap-hit rate, rule-A loop share and accuracy on finished answers. It does not cover T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, where the theory expects few loops at any checkpoint. It does not cover the 3.0 release, the first release (fr-01) or RL-Zero-Code/IF/General/Mix. It makes no claim about weight-difference interpolations theta(a), which are not points on the training path. It does not explain the residual accuracy gap on finished answers at step 2,800.

imports.finding: 73 % of entropy loss and 76 % of the performance gain occur in the first 200 of 2,400 RL steps.
imports.how: Places the entropy collapse and most of the gain on finished answers before step 400, the first phase of the mechanism.

imports.finding: Under top-p with threshold above 1/2, a loop position becomes deterministic once the loop token's probability reaches the threshold; pure sampling never locks.
imports.how: Explains why a sharper, lower-entropy policy loops more at top-p 0.95: more repeated tokens pass the lock threshold. It also explains why the effect should be specific to truncated sampling at T 0.6.

imports.finding: Looping is a low-temperature effect and falls as temperature rises toward 1.0 for every model tested.
imports.how: Treats the early policy's lower entropy as equivalent to lower temperature, which raises looping before any loop-specific training signal has acted.

imports.finding: At T 0.6 the Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0) model has 29.1 % of responses hit the length limit vs 17.8 % for the base.
imports.how: 3.0 masked truncated rollouts, so it lacks the second phase. Its final cap-hit rate staying above the base's is the first phase seen without the correction.

imports.finding: With overlong filtering at a 20k threshold, models clip more often because of repetitive or non-terminating outputs.
imports.how: Supports the second phase: whether truncated rollouts are penalised decides whether repetition is trained out. 3.1, which trains truncations as negatives, removes the loops only slowly.

explains.quote: 73 % of entropy drop and 76 % of the gain
explains.how: The fast early entropy collapse is the first phase, the one that sharpens the policy before loops are penalised.

explains.quote: RL-Zero-Math 76.5/1k at T 0.6 with 29.1% length-limit hits vs 17.8% base
explains.how: An RL-Zero run without truncation negatives (3.0) ends with more cap hits than the base at T 0.6: the rise without the later removal.

explains.quote: not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives)
explains.how: This is the 3.1 training signal that, in the mechanism, slowly removes the loops created early.
By step 2,800 the loops have been trained out, so the final RL model no longer depends on temperature, unlike the base.

explains.quote: Truncating the tail at T 1.0 brings loops back
explains.how: Cutting the low-probability tail, which is what a sharper policy does in effect, brings loops back. This is the link the mechanism needs between lower entropy and more loops.
The same model loops far more at T 0.6 than at T 1.0. Cap hits track the effective sharpness of the sampled distribution.

explains.quote: most of the divergence comes later in training
explains.how: Most of the activation change, which the mechanism links to loop removal, arrives after step 100, which fits a slow second phase.

conflicts.quote: step 100 is at the noise floor
conflicts.how: If the step-100 policy is barely changed, its cap-hit rate may sit at the base's rather than above it. The step-100 half of the rise may then be too small to see.

If these evaluations include early checkpoints, the early policy already scores near the final model, which argues against a phase with many loops. They are, however, at T 1.0 / top-p 0.95 with a 32,768-token cap.

conflicts.quote: a quarter of the RL weight difference gives most of the gain
conflicts.how: A partial step along the final delta gains with no reported loop rise. That is at T 1.0 and off the training path, but it suggests partial RL need not loop.

rival: The rival: 3.1's truncation negatives act from the first steps, so the policy learns to commit and stop at once, and T 0.6 cap hits fall monotonically from the base (65 plain) through steps 100 and 400 to step 2,800. Two observations separate the two. The first is the sign of the step-400-minus-base cap-hit difference on plain MATH-500 and on the harder set at T 0.6: positive here, negative under the rival. The second is what step-400 cap hits are made of: here they are rule-A loops, while under the rival any remaining cap hits are long non-looping deliberation, like RL's 16 loop-free cap hits at T 1.0.

predictions.experiment: Where step 400's accuracy on finished answers lies between base and step 2,800, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, grader v3.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B), .../r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl (M), .../r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (E). In each file keep sample == 0 and, for duplicates, the first row in file order. Keep the problem_index values present in all three files (set S). Grade every row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons grader/rln4_grader_v3.py applied to text and gold); ignore the stored v1 score. For each file, finished = rows in S with cap_hit false (cap_hit missing counts as false only if finish_reason == 'stop'). acc_X = (finished rows with v3 right) / (number of finished rows); empty or unparseable answers count as wrong. Statistic: (acc_M - acc_B) / (acc_E - acc_B). If acc_E - acc_B <= 0, report the statistic as undefined.

predictions.experiment: Share of step-400 cap hits that are rule-A loops, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
predictions.recipe: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl. Keep sample == 0 and, for duplicates, the first row in file order. Keep the rows with cap_hit true (cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length' also counts). For each such row, apply rule A to the text field. For every character position p that is 0 or follows a newline, with at least 8,000 characters from p to the end, take w = text[p:p+8000] and compute r = len(zlib.compress(w.encode('utf-8'))) / len(w.encode('utf-8')), using Python zlib at its default level. The row is a loop if any such r < 0.10. A row with fewer than 8,000 characters is not a loop. Statistic: loop rows / cap-hit rows. If there are no cap-hit rows, the statistic is undefined.

predictions.experiment: Generate allenai/Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math at step_0400 (revision 897c0ce4) with the plain prompt (3.1 chat template, as in the r3 P cells) on MATH-500, n = 500, one sample, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384 new tokens, seed 1,000,000 + problem_index, vLLM on one H100 via jobs/run_cell.py. Grade with grader v3. Compare cap hits with step 400's T 0.6 P_math500 sample-0 rows.
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 405 right of 500, or the T 1.0 cell's cap-hit count is not below the cap-hit count of r3 s0400 P_math500 sample 0 at T 0.6
